plan-fold-the-whole-selection.text: Read the spec for the stories, the rulings and the acceptance, the gate for the checks, the touch list for every file, and the tasks for the commit boundaries.

where-the-work-stands.text: Pull requests 1 and 2 and the docs-only follow-up are merged. Pull request 3 was released on the thirteenth of October against main at e7b55ac9 and is planned below as two pull requests, 3a and 3b, on the branch feat/518-many-per-fold; the bullets below describe the ticket as planned for pull request 1.

strategy.text: The library's fold already speculates every pending request at the request address; it gains an explicit selection, and the validity bound follows the selection. The command chooses the selection purely, from the pending outputs, the live state, the clock and the capacity bound, and carries a list through the receipt, the journal and reconciliation. The selection itself is a pure library module with no command-line and no open-datum import, so a conformance test can ask the model about its output, and the registry's command line and the open-datum executable use it without it knowing either.

three-pull-requests.text: The slice is cut into pull requests that each ship a runnable outcome. The first cut (two pull requests) was made before dispatch; on 2026-10-11 the epic owner ruled a second cut (the desk's option B): the receipt readers and the other pages move behind pull request 1, and the former pull request 2 ("many per fold") becomes pull request 3. The spec and the gate were frozen under the first numbering and still say "2" for what is now pull request 3 (their lines marked 1 are pull request 1, except where the touch list moves a reader or a page to pull request 2). One patch per slice in a patch stack, no journey commits. Each slice builds and passes its candidate gate; hosted CI at the exact head is the net. Merge order: #528, #381, pull request 1, #358 slice 3, pull request 2, then pull request 3.

pull-request-1-each-request-judged-alone.text: Pull request 1: each request judged alone, one settled per fold.
Runnable outcome: with two pending requests, one of them stuck, registry fold settles the other and names the stuck one; the refusal of the 2026-10-07 rehearsal is gone.

pull-request-2-the-receipt-readers-and-t.text: Pull request 2: the receipt readers and the other pages.

Runnable outcome: every reader of a fold receipt reads the list receipt, the top-level single-request fields are gone from the fold receipt and from the combined forms, and the pages state it. Started from main at 9d5f4c7a: pull request 1 merged, and the command-line split merged, so the base is main, by the desk release of 2026-10-11. Behaviour does not change: the bound is still 1; only the shape of the receipt and its readers move.

What goes: the single-request fields request, key, edge, live output, envelope, released and deposit, and the datum hash and datum bytes of a datum delivery, from the receipt of registry fold; the four fold-derived duplicates live output, envelope, released and deposit from the receipts of insert with fold and terminate with fold. What stays at the top level, being facts of the transaction and not of one request: the folder, the fold transaction, the root, the fold deadline, the validity bound slot, the post-build verdict, the host clock, the time remaining, the booking of a combined form and the key fields of a booking, and the three lists. A reader takes a settled request, its key, edge, owner, settlement and deadline from the first entry of the settled list.

Readers on main, found by reading the code and the scripts: the conformance command-line controls and their unit fixtures; the Demo 1 journey script; the command-run specs of the registry and of the open-datum package; the rows of the fold rules spec that pin the earlier fields. The recovery controls script and the control check script read none of the removed fields and are not edited. That search looked for distinctive field names and missed one reader: the two-actor journey script and its status test read the request and the edge of a fold receipt, and three hosted jobs of the first push failed on them. The search is now by what consumes a fold receipt: every file that reads the JSON printed by registry fold, insert with fold or terminate with fold is listed with a verdict, moved, reads only kept fields, or reads no fold receipt, and the two files above join the readers of slice 1. No page shows the removed fields as a receipt example; the node guide states that they are kept, which stops being true.
Slices, one patch each, in this order so that main stays green at each. The lists exist since pull request 1, so a reader can move before the fields go.
Pull request body: names each removed field and each reader moved, under the template interface section, and carries the Principle VII paragraph.

Allowance: 3 hours of writer time, by the desk ruling, with base-forced rebases apart; a race box names writer time and the gate run time separately. Estimate with the observed ratio of 1.4 over a plain estimate: slice 1 about 70 minutes, slice 2 about 50, slice 3 about 45, 165 in all. Writers are one-task runs alternating the two families, with a fresh Codex auditor.

Cut point, named in the plan at the epic owner request: the slice that leaves pull request 2 if the forecast passes the allowance is the other pages, meaning the preprod page, the fold responsibilities page and the rehearsal document, with their speech companions and narration. The owner is the ticket owner of 518, in a docs-only pull request from main after pull request 2 merges, or in the documentation slice of pull request 3 if that starts first. The trigger is mechanical: after each accepted slice the forecast is the writer minutes spent plus the remaining estimates, and if it passes 180 the cut is executed without a question. The slices that stay are the readers, the removal and the node guide sentence, because readers and removal cannot be separated and the guide must say the fields are gone. The three pages state behaviour that has been stale since pull request 1 and does not depend on the removal, so leaving them strands no reader; the body of pull request 2 then names them as a recorded limit. If the forecast still passes 180 with the readers, the removal and the guide alone, that is a question for a longer allowance.

the-command-line-split-528-is-the-base.text: The command-line split (#528) is the base.

#528 makes the Singular command line registry-only, moves the open datum into its own executable and package, and introduces an application value that carries everything the registry needs to know of an application. Its mandate is specs/528-registry-cli-split/ in the repository. #528 has merged (c6748950); this plan was written against the code as #528 left it on its approved heads, and the branch now sits on main.

evidence-this-ticket-produces.text: Receipts: the failing and passing runs of each slice's focused suite; the conformance unit run with its same-key control; the hosted run links for the three executed devnet items (two actors one fold, an excluded request left and named, an interrupted two-request fold reconciled) and for every required check at the exact head. The pull request body is a fill-in of the repository template:

budget-and-size.text: One team per epic at a time; the operator is on credits. The split is decided above with an estimate per pull request, each followed by 60 to 90 minutes of hosted CI that the merge waits for. The estimates of the first cut were 2 to 3 hours of commit-owner time for pull request 1 and 3 to 4 hours for the former pull request 2; the observed ratio over the estimates is about 1.4, 41 of the first 133 minutes came from the stacked base, and the epic owner ruled an allowance of 7.5 hours for pull request 1. Commit owners are launched one task at a time, each with the terminal condition green, blocked or at capacity. Pull requests 2 and 3 are new dispatches after the pull request before them merges. The desk ruled on the session-layer collision on the thirteenth of October, and pull request 3 is released with 240 minutes of writer time, planned as pull request 3a at 155 minutes and pull request 3b at 195 minutes, the second of which needs its own allowance from the epic owner. A pull request that would run past its estimate by a working day is stopped at its last green checkpoint and the remainder is proposed to the epic owner as a question, not ground out.

pull-request-3-many-per-fold-cut-in-two.text: Pull request 3: many per fold, cut in two.

Main already folds a chosen set of requests in the builder and the guards. What is still one request is the fold routine, the journal line and the observation in the reconciliation code. The estimate is about 350 minutes, more than the 240 allowed for each part, so the pull request is cut in two. Pull request 3a makes the fold, the builder and the journal carry a selection of any size while the bound stays 1, and changes nothing a user sees. Pull request 3b recovers a many-request fold, raises the bound to 9 and proves the whole behaviour on a development network. The bound rises only in the pull request that also recovers a many-request fold, so main never holds a fold it cannot recover. The branch stands on the bookkeeping lane's branch, and every push waits for that merge and a rebase onto main.
